summary: Intermittent egress path redistribution in us-west causing streaming token gaps and timeouts for VoxMetrics
description:
Issue summary: VoxMetrics reported intermittent high latency and streaming stalls for long chat sessions originating from their us-west users. Symptoms started around 2026-03-10 08:45 UTC and manifested as P95/P99 increases for token emission and occasional finalization timeouts (120s) causing client-side reconnects.

Impact: A subset of requests (~3-7% of VoxMetrics traffic in us-west) experienced token gaps of 200-600ms and several complete timeouts. This impacted conversational UX and caused increased error rates in the customer’s observability (retries and duplicate messages).

Timeline: 2026-03-10 08:47 UTC - Customer CS pinged support with attached traces. 2026-03-10 09:05 UTC - Support triaged and opened SUP-17789. 2026-03-10 09:30 UTC - Initial SRE check showed transient egress path changes for a subset of nodes in us-west. 2026-03-11 02:15 UTC - Network team confirmed BGP redistribution events observed on provider leg; correlated with route flaps between colo A and transit provider. 2026-03-11 08:00 UTC - Temporary geo-affinity pin applied for VoxMetrics to us-east; partial mitigation observed.

Observed behavior: - Streaming responses show irregular inter-token timing (bursts and long gaps). - Connection-level metrics show elevated retransmits and occasional TLS handshake delays when egress route shifted. - Affected backends were routed over an alternate transit path adding ~90-180ms RTT.

Hypothesis: A provider-side route redistribution caused asymmetric egress paths that increased RTT and jitter. Because our streaming runtime depends on predictable RTT for continuous token pipelining and prefix caching, these path changes cause cache hot-shard misses and delay in inflight KV cache fetches, amplifying visible token gaps and creating hard timeouts for long sessions.

Next steps: 1) Network to work with transit provider to stabilize BGP advertisements for the affected colo. 2) SRE to add short-term egress-path healthcheck and route-blacklist for known-bad transit. 3) Product/Support to keep VoxMetrics updated and monitor P95/P99 for next 48 hours. 4) Follow-up postmortem and possible routing fallback automation RFC.
steps_to_reproduce: From an us-west client, initiate a long streaming generation with context length > 2k tokens against redwood-rlhf-2 and measure inter-token timings for the first 120 seconds.
Run curl against the /v1/streams endpoint repeatedly (50-200 concurrent short-lived connections) to replicate higher multiplexing load and observe p95 token emission.
Compare traceroute and MTR from serving nodes to customer edge IPs during a symptomatic window to spot path changes and per-hop latency increases.
Replay customer trace IDs with internal debug flags enabled to capture KV cache miss rates and scheduler backpressure timestamps.

comments: Aisha Khan (2026-03-10 09:05 UTC): Customer reports repeated token gaps and occasional 120s session timeouts from us-west. Attached their traces and sample request IDs.
Marcus Li (2026-03-10 09:22 UTC): Triage done. Escalated to SRE and Network. Initial signs point to egress path change on a subset of nodes. Queueing full MTRs and BGP dumps.
SRE - Priya Desai (2026-03-10 10:10 UTC): Observed transient route flaps on provider leg for colo-usw-2. Creating INT-4023 for internal tracking with network team.
Network - Javier Morales (2026-03-11 02:18 UTC): Confirmed redistribution event from transit provider between 01:40-02:10 UTC. We requested route dampening and are awaiting provider acknowledgement.

Support - Aisha Khan (2026-03-11 08:10 UTC): Applied temporary geo-affinity pin for VoxMetrics to route them through us-east while provider works on stabilization. Customer reports reduced p95 but still occasional spikes.
VoxMetrics - Elena Park (Customer, 2026-03-11 08:30 UTC): Noted improvement after pin; still see 2-3% of sessions with token gaps. Requesting follow-up and permanent fix timeline.
investigation_notes: MTRs show extra 3-4 hops when alt path used; additional per-hop latency ~25-40ms each leading to +90-180ms RTT.
KV cache miss rate increased by ~8% for affected traces during redistribution window; suggests cache affinity broken by path change.
No increase in CPU/GPU utilization on serving nodes during incidents — points to network rather than runtime overload.
Internal INT-4023 includes BGP dumps and provider contact thread: provider acknowledged abnormal L2/peering config change and is preparing a rollback.
Potential longer-term mitigation: implement egress-path health scoring and automatic sticky-affinity fallback to alternate stable transit or region.
Consider adding a streaming runtime adjustment to tolerate RTT spikes by increasing internal per-token timeouts for pinned sessions.
workaround: Applied geo-affinity pin to route VoxMetrics traffic to us-east for affected customers and reduced aggressive prefetch on streaming runtime for pinned sessions. This reduced visible P95 by ~60% for the customer. Continue monitoring for 48 hours.
resolution: Mitigation in place (geo-affinity pin + provider dampening request). Awaiting provider confirmation of permanent fix and SRE follow-up to implement egress health checks and automation. Postmortem scheduled upon provider resolution and internal RFC for fallback automation.
notes_for_postmortem: Collect full BGP dumps for 2026-03-10 01:30-03:00 UTC window from colo-usw-2.
Quantify customer impact across tenants in us-west for same window (p95/p99 deltas).
Design RFC for egress route scoring and automated geo-affinity failover.
Evaluate streaming runtime changes to tolerate short-term RTT spikes (configurable token timeout).
Engage transit provider for remediation timeline and potential SLA credits if root cause confirmed on provider side.
